title: Joint vs. Combined operations
studentMustDo: Distinguish JOINT (US services only) from COMBINED (US plus partner/allied nations) operations.

title: Command authorities — COCOM/OPCON/TACON/ADCON
studentMustDo: Identify the correct command authority for tasking coalition forces; explain what each authority allows and what it does not.

title: ADCON in coalition operations
studentMustDo: Explain how administrative control (ADCON) is retained by the national/service force even when units operate under another commander's OPCON or TACON.

title: TACS layers and CAS request chain
studentMustDo: Identify the three layers of the Theater Air Control System and route a Close Air Support request from ground commander to aircraft.

title: AWACS vs. JSTARS
studentMustDo: Differentiate AWACS (airborne air picture) from JSTARS (airborne ground picture) and identify what each detects.

title: TAC(A) vs. FAC(A) and TACP/JTAC
studentMustDo: Distinguish TAC(A) coordination from FAC(A) terminal control; identify the JTAC within the TACP as the person qualified to control weapons delivery.

title: AOC products and producing divisions
studentMustDo: Match each AOC product (ATO, MAAP, AOD, ACO, SPINS, JAOP) to its producing division and rank by planning horizon.

title: Liaison elements — BCD, NALE, SOLE
studentMustDo: Route requests from land, maritime, and SOF components to the correct AOC liaison element.

title: JFACC vs. AOC
studentMustDo: Distinguish the JFACC (commander) from the AOC (headquarters) and explain the relationship between them.

title: JAOP vs. AOD
studentMustDo: Differentiate the long-range Joint Air Operations Plan from the cycle-specific Air Operations Directive and sequence them in the air tasking cycle.

title: ISR Strategists in SRD
studentMustDo: Identify the embedded ISR position that supports SRD with PIR development and collection alignment.

title: Assessment feedback loop
studentMustDo: Trace BDA and assessment products back from COD execution to SRD/CPD for the next planning cycle.

title: CPD teams and their products
studentMustDo: Match each CPD team (TET, C2 Planning, MAAP Team, ATO Production) to the planning task it handles and the product it delivers.

title: MAAP vs. ATO
studentMustDo: Sequence MAAP before ATO; explain MAAP as the blueprint and ATO as the executable order.

title: Collateral damage estimation in CPD
studentMustDo: Identify the CPD team responsible for Collateral Damage Estimation (CDE) prior to target inclusion.

title: COD execution floor positions
studentMustDo: Identify the COD positions and teams (CCO, Offensive Ops, Defensive Ops, ACF, ICT, ISRDO) and what each handles in execution.

title: CCO personal authority
studentMustDo: Identify which dynamic execution decisions require the CCO's personal authority (ROE, time-sensitive targeting).

title: Dynamic targeting and TST
studentMustDo: Define dynamic targeting and apply it to Time-Sensitive Targets not on the ATO.

title: ISRDO cross-division relationship
studentMustDo: Explain why the ISRDO sits on the COD floor while organizationally belonging to ISRD (dashed-line relationship).

title: ISRD cells and their functions
studentMustDo: Identify each ISRD cell (ACF, ISR Operations Team, CMC) and the function it performs.

title: ISRD across the AOC
studentMustDo: Describe how ISRD supports SRD (ISR Strategists), CPD (CMC / RSTA Annex), and COD (ISRDO embedded on the floor).

title: PED and the RSTA Annex
studentMustDo: Define Processing, Exploitation, and Dissemination (PED); identify the ISRD cell that produces the RSTA Annex.

title: AMD core missions
studentMustDo: Identify the three core AMD missions: Airlift, Air Refueling, and Aeromedical Evacuation.

title: Air refueling coordination
studentMustDo: Route a tanker shortfall to the correct AMD team for re-allocation.

title: Airlift mission planning
studentMustDo: Identify the AMD team responsible for airlift mission planning and integration with the ATO.

title: AECT — Aeromedical Evacuation Control Team
studentMustDo: Identify the AECT as the AMD team that owns Aeromedical Evacuation planning and execution.

title: AE vs. CSAR — critical distinction
studentMustDo: Distinguish Aeromedical Evacuation (AMD / AECT, permissive environment, medical transport) from Combat Search and Rescue (COD / PRCC, hostile environment, combat recovery) and identify the handoff point.
